questions.q: A contestable market is best described as one where:
options: Entry and exit are easy, so the threat of entry affects behaviour
questions.why: What counts is the threat, not the number of firms.

options: Costs that can't be recovered if a firm leaves the market
questions.why: They make entering and leaving riskier.

questions.q: Hit-and-run competition is more likely when sunk costs are high.
questions.why: A firm can only leave cheaply if it doesn't lose much on exit.

questions.q: Which market is likely to be the MOST contestable?
questions.why: It needs little capital, and the costs can largely be recovered.

questions.q: As a market becomes more contestable, we would expect:
options: Prices to move closer to average cost
questions.why: The threat of entry limits what firms can charge.

questions.q: Explain how high sunk costs reduce the contestability of a market.

ideas.label: A firm would lose those costs if it left
So entry is riskier, and the threat of entry is weaker

questions.model: Sunk costs cannot be recovered if a firm leaves, so entering is riskier. Fewer firms will enter, the threat of entry is weaker and existing firms can charge more.
questions.why: If you can't leave cheaply, you think twice about entering.

tests.answer: Sunk costs can't be recovered if a firm leaves, so entry is risky and the threat of entry is weak.
